problem_text:
A logistics company needs to distribute its total shipping volume across 12 regional distribution centers to maximize overall delivery efficiency. The operational characteristics for each center are as follows:
* Center A: efficiency score 0.089, operational complexity 0.243, capacity range [0.041, 0.614]
* Center B: efficiency score 0.173, operational complexity 0.207, capacity range [0.005, 0.720]
* Center C: efficiency score 0.164, operational complexity 0.063, capacity range [0.026, 0.357]
* Center D: efficiency score 0.137, operational complexity 0.120, capacity range [0.031, 0.697]
* Center E: efficiency score 0.163, operational complexity 0.114, capacity range [0.070, 0.449]
* Center F: efficiency score 0.040, operational complexity 0.018, capacity range [0.068, 0.507]
* Center G: efficiency score 0.145, operational complexity 0.208, capacity range [0.077, 0.706]
* Center H: efficiency score 0.031, operational complexity 0.253, capacity range [0.058, 0.531]
* Center I: efficiency score 0.190, operational complexity 0.292, capacity range [0.057, 0.803]
* Center J: efficiency score 0.049, operational complexity 0.048, capacity range [0.098, 0.635]
* Center K: efficiency score 0.095, operational complexity 0.277, capacity range [0.067, 0.893]
* Center L: efficiency score 0.126, operational complexity 0.043, capacity range [0.034, 0.333]

Each center must handle a proportion of the total shipping volume that stays within its individual capacity limits, and all proportions must sum to one. To maintain adequate operational readiness, the company requires that the group of high-readiness centers, represented by the subset R = {A, B, D, H, I, J, L}, collectively handle at least 0.379 of the total volume. Additionally, the overall operational complexity index must not exceed 0.196, and the total efficiency score must be no less than 0.076. Determine the optimal volume allocation that maximizes the total efficiency score while satisfying all constraints.
